reviewScope: Functional population aggregation 13.7, with all five actual language implementations and readonly Country bindings.

questions.algorithm: Lambda-based continent filtering and population summation, using a fused conditional accumulate in C++ and the actual language pipeline elsewhere.
questions.review: Read pinned Java Country and QuestionA/QuestionB sources, then all five independently authored bodies. Provided Country objects expose actual getters; the private wire-tuple decoder is not passed to candidates. Exact continent contents, not country name or object identity, determine membership. Nonnegative populations and the 1000-by-million bound keep each actual int/Number sum exact. C# lazy Where/Sum, Java sequential filter/mapToInt/sum and Python lazy filter/map/sum do not materialize matching lists. C++ folds with a readonly capturing lambda over a const vector reference. JavaScript filter intentionally allocates matching references before reduce and its O(m) temporary storage is stated. Independent scalar-loop oracle covers exhaustive small occurrence lists, zero/no matches, duplicates, case/space distinctions, composed/decomposed accents, emoji and maximum billion total. Child observations check original array member identity/order and Country getter values; C++ supplied model fields and input reference are readonly. Five actual reordering variants retain the correct sum but fail mutation checks; five unfiltered-total variants fail result semantics. Neutral zero-return starters are executed and rejected, not credited from presence checks.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Read Country[] binding and immutable private Country fields/getters. String operator == compares contents ordinally. Where plus selector Sum is lazy and uses a bounded int accumulator; array elements are snapshotted by reference identity before invocation.
languageBindingReview.java: Read Country[] binding, final model fields and String.equals membership. Sequential Arrays.stream/filter/mapToInt/sum carries primitive int populations without a matching-record array. Input references and getter triples are observed before and after.
languageBindingReview.cpp: Read const vector<Country>& and const string& callable parameters, const getters and the std::accumulate lambda capture. The zero identity is int under the proven total bound, no Country copies are made in the actual fold, and input values/order are independently projected afterward.
languageBindingReview.python: Read list[Country] binding and private getter-backed fields. filter/map are lazy and sum consumes them with zero identity. Observation rejects bool-as-int, input membership/reordering and changed getter values; Unicode matching is exact without normalization.
languageBindingReview.javascript: Read actual Country objects with private # fields and getters. filter creates a fresh array of original matching references; reduce starts at 0 and preserves original input references. Number sums are exact under the admitted bound and strict equality preserves case/Unicode distinctions.
